title: Dave Canales: 'With change comes opportunity' | Carolina Panthers
text: It's a great weekend for us all to get together , you know, with the recent changes on the defensive side, to put our heads together and make sure our guys are in a great position to succeed. Trying to highlight some of the talents and skills of the kids we have there.  And, well, we just had another defensive meeting.  I was able to speak with some of the leadership council this morning, and then the entire defense team met today just to discuss a few things and make sure we're on the same page going forward. Incredible.  Thank you, coach. We'll start with Mike and then with Joe. Hello, hello Dave. What's up, Mike? You mentioned, well, the last time we spoke with you you mentioned considering changes to the offensive line . Where are you at with that position, and also what kinds of challenges come with having free time and explaining what your process is? Yes, Mike, your voice is breaking up, but I heard the questions.  First of all , regarding the offensive line, it's something we 're still discussing.  I do n't really want to go into details about what that looks like , but I will say this: Brady Christensen, let's open up his 21-day window so we can see where he stands from a footballing perspective.  He's healthy, strong, fit and ready to play, but we need to get him into game rhythm here. So that will be a good addition to the group to assess where it can potentially help us. But as for the rest of the group, we know collectively as a team that, from the coaching staff to the quarterback groups, the offensive line working on some different things in the passing game, it's something we 're thinking about and working on right now. Um, regarding the other part of the question, I think you simply mean having this time;  And it really came at a good time so that we could join forces and have a few extra days in the building to work on different things I have in mind regarding our style of play and the various ways of employing our players on the defensive side. Hi Dave, how are you? Hi Joe. I was wondering about that 21- day window, do you plan to do the same for X and Jonathan Brooks as well? Yes, we're still considering all of that as well.  At this moment, Brady is probably the one returning in the best position of that group.  So we'll start with Brady.  We continue to evaluate the rest of the guys to determine when that window will be. That?  So, are you saying it wouldn't be this week, or potentially yes? Potentially.  We need to see them on the field, see a couple of different things from JB and also from Xavier. And time is running out on us very quickly.  So we need to be able to evaluate.  Fortunately, we have a little extra time to meet with those boys and decide how to proceed. And do you have any idea about Jaylen's availability for this week?   It's going in the right direction.  I feel like it's something that happens every day. Um, it reached good speeds for us.  But again, with the new injury in the same area, that's where we really need to make sure he's ready to handle not just a couple of isolated high speeds, but the volume required to play a match You know, in my opinion, when you want a player to return, you have to be able to say that he can handle his normal workload , rather than, you know, occasions where in certain positions you might say, " Hey, maybe it's 30-40% workload." But I want Jaylen to feel safe , to feel that he can go out there and do his job like he always does. Thank you. Yes. Great, we'll go with Eric and then with Jeff. Coach, how are you? Good.  And you? Good, friend.  Excellent.  Of course, there was the news this morning about DeAngelo Hall's return to the coaching staff here in Carolina.  He talks about, you know, what he brings to the table and what he can ultimately do for a really young group of cornerbacks Honestly, I'm very lucky that D-Hall is here.   You know, he's in Charlotte with his family and we were able to have some very productive conversations, right before Cooley left, and he was excited. So, we were talking and suddenly we have a guy with a lot of playing experience, someone excited to coach, to make an impact on our group and challenge these guys to keep progressing. So, I'm very fortunate to have D-Hall's energy, experience, and all of that back in the building. And well, looking forward to this weekend's matchup against Denver, a team that, obviously, always remains competitive in games. What do you think could pose the biggest challenge for the team this weekend? Well, it's simply the attitude with which they play;  Coach Payton does a great job with this group. Defensively speaking, they have been very consistent in recent years with Vance Joseph and the style of play he has managed to implement.  On the offensive side , they rely more on their running game, but there are also the big plays that Bo manages to create, coming out of the pocket and finding talent downfield, because of how they use their skilled players.  It's a balanced attack, it's complete team football.  I didn't mention their team of specialists, but they play a good level of football, which always gives you a chance to win. Thank you, coach. Mhm. Good afternoon, coach.  Can you hear me?   I'm listening, Jeff. Brilliant. Penalties remain a problem.   A few weeks ago, you defended the aggressive nature of the penalties.   Do you still think the same or are you starting to worry about how often you use tissues ?   I mean , aside from the franchise record of 15 penalties in one day, we've been pretty close to the expected average. When I see the boys committing fouls due to exertion, we can correct their technique.  What we cannot allow are the things that happen after the whistle. Certainly, some of the penalties for decision-making that occurred are things we can correct.  But, Jeff, I want our boys to play fast. I want them to play aggressively. You know, Will Lee had a couple of handkerchiefs thrown at him in Philly and, you know, I supported him because he was challenging the rivals.  I was right on top of them, and you ca n't get those penalties unless you're right there with great coverage.  So I want these guys to be aggressive, but I also want them to grow and learn where they are and how to make a play on the ball the right way. And following that, Marco Wilson had that emotional penalty, a roughness foul away from the ball. Is that an example of being too aggressive? Absolutely.  Yes, Marco and I talked about that right after.  I didn't want to draw attention to it because he was really challenging those guys.  He was challenging them at the beginning of the routes, being physical with his hands. I want our boys to be able to play that way.  And after the play, especially when you're in the back far away from her, that's where we need to have discipline.  We cannot give the opponent anything, any kind of advantage that way.  So that's something we definitely talked about. And what do you expect from Wilson this week? Could he be the starting cornerback ? Marco will be out there.  You know, he showed us that he has potential.  And their movement skills, their aggressive nature, their confidence, all those things out there are exactly what we're looking for. And he will continue to improve as we delve deeper into our concepts. Hey, thanks.  Good luck. Thank you.   We'll go with Mike Solarte and then with Alex First, coach. Hi, Mike. I hope you had a good weekend.  I hope you had a good weekend. We spoke to you on Friday, right after the changes in the coaching staff.  The players had a little time.  You had a little time too. What has been the reaction now that everyone has returned after a couple of days and is starting to refocus for the week? It was an appropriate reaction.  You know , these are two coaches, E and Cooley , people I respect a lot, who I enjoyed working with, and who also meant a lot to the players.  So it's an appropriate reaction; there was some sadness, and for me, this feels like a loss.   It was certainly a difficult weekend , but at the same time, we must move forward, focus and determine what we will do collectively, and the players are ready for that too. Understanding that the match is this Sunday.  Let's focus on the Denver Broncos.  Let's talk about how we'll play defense so we can advance.  So it's a good combination of both.  Mike, thanks for asking, it's not something I take lightly, and neither do the guys .  And that's because it's a very close- knit group that enjoys coming to work together.  That's why it will always have that kind of impact. And one last question from me about the division. Your smile tells me a little bit about what you're thinking.   I mean, it's kind of crazy, but the fact that you guys have a record of three and four and are leading the table, with everything you have ahead of you, how do you approach the next 10 games?   I know they're going one by one, but they also need to think about the bigger picture. Yes, the approach is week by week. You said it, and the question is: how much longer can we maintain this statement as true?  We are in first place in the division with our entire destiny before us.  This next game is just as important as the rest of them.  Therefore, having the mindset to find that consistency we seek is our goal in all areas and in all three phases of the game. And with the urgency of this moment and those decisions made, it really increases the pressure on all of us as staff and for our dressing room, to decide to find that consistent football we are looking for and win that first championship, which is the division. Hey Dave, you mentioned Will Levis a moment ago.  What is the status of your injury? Yes, day by day.   You know, we did some assessments.   I won't give, you know, the full picture of the injuries.  We'll have it ready by Wednesday. But we're in a day-to-day situation with him, honestly.  So he's in rehab.  It is evolving in the right direction.  We'll have a few opportunities this week to try it out and see how it feels. Understood.  And when we spoke to you last Friday, you mentioned that this change in defense is intended, in part, to highlight the best qualities of your defensive team, your defensive personnel.   Are there any particular players who expect to benefit from this move? There are certainly several.  I just don't want to go into details about what that will look like because, you know, at this point it's something we're working on and, again, it's a competitive advantage for us to be able to work on it without talking about it.  So, excellent.  We'll go with Darren and Vasha. Yes, Dave, you mentioned meeting with the veterans council earlier today. What are those meetings like, and what did you take away from that group environment? Yes, without going into specific details of the conversation, it's something we do quarterly where we bring that group together.  And you know, the first thing I want to know is: what do you need from me as your head coach? The way we do things in terms of scheduling, the way we communicate, you know, and really reviewing our processes is because I need your support.  I need your help to be able to, uh, replicate the message of how we prepare, how we practice, and how our week unfolds so that we arrive on Sunday confident and ready to play.  So we reviewed many of those things. Um, and then I give them my opinion, I gave them a broad perspective on the decisions made and the expectations I have for our staff and also for our wardrobe. And, uh, asking the guys to make sure that at this moment, you know, with change comes opportunity , to really emphasize the urgency in how we do things in all aspects. And, um, asking them to really support that part and do their part to contribute to it. Do your part each week, and I've told you this from the beginning, is that I will ask you for more, and not necessarily to do more things, but to put more effort into what we already do to master them , to master our processes, to master our fundamentals. All the communication, the communication line, and all those things that happen.  So it was a great opportunity to challenge the guys in that way and also to see how they felt.   Do you remember anything in particular, perhaps from past seasons, where you heard something in that environment that you later implemented in the show? Yes, there have been quite a few;  Sometimes it was about our meeting times and what works for the whole group, and I usually ask them: how many of you feel the same way?  Just to see if there's any way to find an edge, a way to better prepare our lads, whether it's through recovery, meeting times, or whatever is necessary;  working together and understanding that I didn't always make those changes, but there were some that worked better for us and that we still maintain.  And also, in general terms, I want to hear from them as well.  Where are we at right now , guys?  You guys know the locker room atmosphere much better than I do. You are in there. How is the group feeling right now , in terms of personal connection, attention to detail, the effort you're putting in, and all that? How does it feel for you? Is this an acceptable standard of play we're at now?  And if not, what can we do to improve it? Or do they really like what's happening here?  Brilliant.  Let's keep pushing on those things.  So it's a good exchange of ideas. Hi, Dave. That answer has just opened up another question.  How sincere are these meetings? Are they really that direct? They are very productive and very direct.  And at different times during the last two and a half years, almost two and a half years , sometimes they are a little more emotional and other times more practical, simply talking about specific things that we can adjust or improve. But they've meant a lot to me because I understand the importance of the influence these guys have in the locker room, especially when you add young players, draft picks, and guys who are still developing and trying to figure out how to be professionals, to have a good process for how they recover , how they prepare, and other things like that And then, they are the ones who can be on the other side of, uh, where you have your technical staff.  And it's our job to help them with their development, but then you have these veteran leaders who know how to do it and have a process.  So I asked them, " Guys, let them learn what you do well so they can incorporate it into their daily lives."  So, uh, they've been, you know, really productive meetings. Oh, and my real question was, I know you said this was a difficult decision for you.  I'm curious, from a personal point of view, how was this weekend for you? Were there many meetings with the coaches? Did you have time to reflect? Like, what, what, what have you been doing this weekend? Yes, it was basically daily, you know, going back to the office as defensive staff and, you know, what might normally amount to some time off, when you play a Thursday game you almost have a mini week off. Uh, we were here talking, sorting things out, talking about our players first and foremost, talking about our schemes. Uh, you know, the things that, the things that will allow us to be at our best level.  Uh, so we did that a lot.  And, uh, and then beyond that part, there was also a lot of time to just think about the whole thing and why now.  And, uh, and you know, the urgency I feel with this group of talent that, you know, Dan, myself, and Brant have built up in this locker room , uh, and trying to make sure we do the best for those guys.  But, and then certainly, just a lot, a lot of thinking about personal relationships and, uh, how things change when there is, when I make a decision like this. Hmm, how those dynamics change, so for me it's a loss, you know, and it's something personal that I don't take lightly and it affects more people than just me. It affects other people on this work team.  People who have known each other for a long time, but I have an obligation to make sure I put our players in the best possible situation for this team this year.  And that's what really led to the decision We'll wrap up with John and then with Mike K. Hi Dave, happy Monday to you.  How are you? Fine, thanks. Excellent.  Just one question about your history in the NFL. We know you were with Pete Carroll, so maybe that's the obvious answer, but which defensive-minded coach had the biggest influence on your current defensive philosophies, and do you see this perhaps as a return to some things you really believe in defensively? Is that the idea behind this change, to some extent?  Just a little bit of history about how you see the game defensively. Without going into details, these are simply the principles of being committed to stopping the ground game. And then, what that looks like for our group based on what we currently have, what we've practiced, what we worked on throughout the offseason and training camp, and our staff. And, you know, being built as a 3-4 defense, from a basic point of view , is what works best for us to be able to play well against the run.  And that philosophical aspect comes from Pete. And that commitment to do that, to play a physical style of football, one that we can count on. And I won't go into detail about everything else, but it was certainly 14 years with Pete and understanding what was most important. It's the ground game.  It's about eliminating explosive plays and going after the ball , however we can. Dave, just one more question about steals.  They had three in the game against Green Bay.  What seems to be a trend, at least from my point of view, is the lack of conversion of those steals into points .  What does that conversation look like in your meeting rooms? Absolutely.  And that's something that I, Brad, uh, the offensive staff, you know , are connected in that way where, you know, even, you know, the night before the game, with a plus one on the turnover margin for us as the Panthers, we have an 80% win rate. That was the 20% right there, where you win the turnover battle, but you don't win the game.  That's because we don't convert that into points.  So, uh, it's definitely something we 're talking about.  And um, you know, we're just, uh, coming up with a plan.  And that just fits into the whole picture, offensively speaking, of , you know, making sure we get back to a place where we can be balanced and , um, where we can run the ball, shoot with action, you know, when we fall back and get into our, um, our open game and those different things, that we're handling the pressure the right way.  And it's not just blitzes, but also stunts.  It's about four-man pressure and making sure we're getting enough help where we need it on tackles.  Um, that the rhythms of the passes fit together in the right way.  So , all of those are things that influence making sure we create, uh, and score points by getting those recoveries Thanks, Dave. I hope, uh, technology doesn't fail me this time, but with D'Angelo, when you were making that decision, did you consult with Mike, Jack, and JC, guys who have been close to him, Todd, Wyatt? Why is this a good opportunity for him, when I mean after he left in 2025, it wasn't? Yes, it's just, you know, my personal observation of D Hall and the way he , you know, will bravely challenge, you know, the status quo and ask, you know , ask the guys to play certain techniques, to express their opinions That's something I really value. People who aren't afraid to offer their experience, their knowledge, you know, just the different things that are important to them. Um, and so, just knowing that, like knowing his heart to want to help these guys, the development and all that, uh, for me it was just like his name was the first name that came to mind when I was thinking about making sure we have enough coaching coverage for our players, where Ronaldo takes care of all the secondary, but then we can have someone continuing to develop the outside cornerbacks. He is still developing as a coach.  Ronaldo has obviously developed and followed a similar path.  How much can he learn from Ronaldo?  We can't talk to him very often, but Mike, how can Ronaldo also help him grow as a coach? Yes, this is invaluable and it is our commitment to development.   Being able to connect with someone who has been in multiple systems;  Um, understanding how to use tools, how to prepare for the week, and, you know, planning a great aerial game plan, putting the guys in a mindset where they anticipate what's going to happen based on the formation, the spread, and the down and distance situation—all of those things will be very valuable for D Hall as he continues, you know, to progress down this path.  And right now , I just need him to coach the cornerbacks and he'll learn a lot of those things in the conversations as we go along.

text: The Jets had a chance to beat the Raiders and then well, you know what happened. Rich Cabini, Jake has been with you. Jet Collective, we're here to break it down. It starts right now. Like the the quality teams in the league, they win one-sore games. Most teams play one-score score games. That's the league. And under Aaron Glenn, they're one and five this year in one-score games. And again, they melt down anytime they've needed to make that big play, whether it be on offense, not settling for a field goal, but actually scoring touchdowns, or whether it be on defense. They've had multiple chances in some of these games to get a big stop and either get the ball back to the offense or close out a team. They don't do it. And I think that's the most obvious sign of a team that is a one, a bad team, but two, a poorly coached team when you routinely fail in the big moments. Well, didn't I read a stat today that the Broncos have won like 15 straight one-score games or or something something of that nature? And the Jets have lost five games by a total of 25 points. And you know the I'm I'm sure Aaron Glenn is looking at that and telling Woody Johnson um we're just that close. You know, we're this close away. And yeah, I mean on paper they're close in those games, but it's the old cliche, so close yet so far. Because I think twothirds of the games in the NFL are one-score games, and that that's what separates the good from the bad. I mean, if you can win most of your one, you're not going to win them all, but if you win most of your one-score games, you're probably going to be in the playoffs. And the Jets just have a propensity to self-destruct in high leverage situations. I think a lot of it is mindset almost like expecting bad things to happen from the player perspective and also as you touched on Jake I think a lot of it is coaching knowing situationally how to respond in certain situations you know what they are short yardage goal line red zone twominute third down all those things the Jets are leaking oil in those areas and that's why they've lost these close games >> every single time you just expect them to lose I mean I now watch these games I'm like Well, how are they going to blow this? And even, as you brought up, when they were up nine, I didn't think they were safe just cuz they were up nine. You knew the Raiders were going to get the ball to start the second half. And the Jets defense, which you know, Aaron Glenn tried to talk about how good they were at the beginning of the year. It was fool's gold. They played Tennessee week one. Cam Ward is not any good. They played the Packers when their offensive line was a total mess and they were down multiple starters, including Josh Jacobs, in a in a monsoon that day at Metife. The Browns game was a monsoon. And I just keep keep coming back to the fact Rich chancing Detroit to get a big stop. They don't do it. The the Bears game never had a chance from the beginning. New England gashed. Never had a chance to get the ball back. Like it just anytime they've had chances. Miami, they're not this great team. They were winless. And you knew they were running the ball with Ali Gordon at the end. Couldn't get the big stop. And yesterday, even though they technically got the ball back and they still bungled the Hail Mary, we can get into that, I'm sure. It's just like every time this defense has had a chance to make Aaron Glenn look smart. That play calling actually is his superpower, they fail. And they and again losing back-to-back games to rookie head coaches when you were a favorite at home. I doubt that has ever happened. And that's what Aaron Glenn now has added to his illustrious resume as the Jet head coach. >> Yeah, they added more games to they extended Kirk Cousins's career a little bit. I think Kirk Cousins was the highest rated passer this week in the NFL in terms of QBR. And I think last week Malik Willis might have been at the top or, you know, very near the top in QBR. All thanks to the Jet defense. These are not high-powered offenses. Now, now Brock Bowers is a sensational player. I I think he's a generational tight end. And the the Raiders used him very smartly. I don't know if you picked up, it's a little wrinkle. Cousins and Powers played pitch and catch for most of the game, two touchdowns, and the Jets defense is uh is just it's not good. I mean, they just have they've given up 30 points a game over the last three and it's uh they are really really struggling. The superpower has met its cryptonite. >> It's just I mean the jokes write themselves. I mean, the second half yesterday, Vegas had 236 yards and they scored four touchdowns. And like again, the Jets wasted and I know the offense certainly wasn't perfect and I'm critical of, you know, their inability to score touchdowns in the red zone. Obviously, we'll get to Brillin Allen's breakout and his role now going forward with the Bruce Hall uncertainty, but you score that many points, no matter how it looks, you have to win the game. The talent's better, sure, but this team is as poorly coached as they were last year. Uh, >> it was the first one in the NFL this year, too, right? >> First one. First one this year, you know, and it's the Jets that give it up. That's that's another put that on the under the checklist of mind-boggling things. But I will say this one thing on defense. They don't have a lot of talent on defense. Now, I know we're going to get on Aaron Glenn and whatever. Look at the defense, Jake. It's just one this year. And you've had moments again like some of the best defenses in the league. They might allow yards, but do they come up with takeaways? Do they have the the the big strip sack when the game's on the line? Like again, like you see defenses give up a lot of yards and points all over the sport, but they make the big play late. The great coaching adjustment and the adjustment was made by the Raiders yesterday because their offense looked completely different whenever they figured out what Glenn and the Jet defense was doing.
